situation.roe_position: Return on equity is currently pulled down by mark-to-market losses on a large fixed-income book. Nine-month 2026 income to common was $777.4 million, with Q3 a net loss of $161.4 million on $879.8 million of mark-to-market losses. Underlying earnings are strong: a 75.1% nine-month combined ratio, with favorable prior-year reserve releases helping. 2025's 26.9% return was lifted by $1.18 billion of investment gains and $1.09 billion of favorable reserve development. Casualty and Specialty loses money underwriting, and Q3 carried $191 million of large-loss events. Falling premiums point to a softening market. Heavy buybacks are shrinking common equity.
situation.why: The company is buying back about $1 billion of stock a year while book value per share rises. This means regulatory capital is not binding and growth is set by management's payout choices and underwriting opportunities. Common equity at 30 Sep 2026 (about $10.6 billion after removing $750 million of preference shares) is already below the 2025 close, because buybacks exceed retained earnings. The 2025 base-year ROE is above a through-cycle level, so I fade it down toward a mid-teens figure, then toward about 12%.

risks.risk: Hard market softens faster than expected, with falling premiums (9M gross premiums written already down) and weaker cat pricing, so ROE reverts toward the cost of equity.

situation.roe_position: FY2025 ROE of 0.2694 was boosted by favourable prior-year reserve releases, a soft-but-still-attractive cat pricing cycle and investment gains. In 2026 underwriting is still strong (9M combined ratio 75.1%), but Q3 GAAP income was a loss because fixed-income mark-to-market losses of $879.8m hit as yields rose. Operating ROE of 18.9% for Q3 includes about 9 points of large-loss drag. Premiums are shrinking and the cycle is softening, so I fade ROE from the high-20s toward the mid-teens. Investment income is supported by a 5.8% portfolio yield.
situation.why: 2025 was an unusually good year: it carried large reserve releases and about $1.2bn of investment gains. Regulatory capital does not appear to bind, since 9M-2026 buybacks of $1,012.6m exceeded common income of $777.4m and common equity fell. Book growth is therefore set by management's payout choice, which depends on how much capital the underwriting cycle lets it deploy.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P5, and S0
business_model.claim: RenaissanceRe is a Bermuda-headquartered global provider of property, casualty, and specialty reinsurance and certain insurance solutions, focusing predominantly on writing reinsurance for customers principally through intermediaries.
quotes: We provide property, casualty and specialty reinsurance and certain insurance solutions to customers, principally through intermediaries.
Established in 1993, and headquartered in Bermuda, we have offices across North America, Europe, and the Asia-Pacific region.
Our current business strategy focuses predominantly on writing reinsurance.

business_model.claim: The company markets its insurance and reinsurance products worldwide through a limited number of brokers, with Aon plc, Marsh & McLennan Companies, Inc., and Arthur J. Gallagher accounting for 81.3% of gross premiums written.
quotes: We market our insurance and reinsurance products worldwide through a limited number of insurance and reinsurance brokers, with three brokerage firms (Aon plc, Marsh & McLennan Companies, Inc. and Arthur J. Gallagher) accounting for 81.3% of our gross premiums written.

business_model.claim: Operations are organized into the Property and the Casualty and Specialty reportable segments, alongside an Other category.
quotes: Our business consists of the following reportable segments: (1) Property, which is comprised of catastrophe and other property (re)insurance, and (2) Casualty and Specialty, which is comprised of general casualty, professional liability, credit and other specialty (re)insurance.
In addition to our two reportable segments, we have an Other category.

business_model.claim: In full-year 2025, Casualty and Specialty generated 6,796,279 (57.9%) and Property generated $4,942,141 (42.1%) of the company's $11,738,420 total gross premiums written (table in thousands).
quotes: The following table shows gross premiums written by segment.

business_model.claim: For the year ended December 31, 2025, Property gross premiums written comprised Catastrophe at $3,318,186 (67.1%) and Other property at 1,623,955 (32.9%), while Casualty and Specialty comprised Other specialty at 2,349,171 (34.6%), General casualty at $2,145,495 (31.6%), Credit at 1,224,716 (18.0%), and Professional liability at 1,076,897 (15.8%) (tables in thousands).

business_model.claim: Across segments, RenaissanceRe writes excess of loss, proportional, and delegated authority business, with proportional and delegated authority contracts carrying higher premiums per unit of expected underwriting income, higher acquisition expense ratios, and higher combined ratios due to more frequent attritional losses and lower expected severity than traditional excess of loss reinsurance.
quotes: Across our segments, we write proportional business, excess of loss business, and business through delegated authority arrangements.

Proportional and delegated authority business typically have relatively higher premiums per unit of expected underwriting income as well as a higher acquisition expense ratio and combined ratio than traditional excess of loss reinsurance, as these coverages tend to be exposed to relatively more attritional, and frequent, losses while being subject to less expected severity.

business_model.claim: Coverages are diversified geographically, with the largest historical exposure in the U.S. and Caribbean, which in the year ended December 31, 2025 accounted for $3,162,323 (26.9%) of total gross premiums written in Property and 3,127,671 (26.6%) in Casualty and Specialty (table in thousands).
quotes: Our exposures are generally diversified across geographic zones, but are also a function of market conditions and opportunities.
Our largest exposure has historically been to the U.S. and Caribbean.

business_model.claim: RenaissanceRe generates earnings through three principal profit drivers—underwriting income, fee income, and investment income—and measures long-term financial success primarily via growth in tangible book value per common share plus the change in accumulated dividends.
quotes: We have three principal drivers of profit that generate diversified earnings streams for our business: underwriting income, fee income, and investment income.
Compared to underwriting income, we view fee income, especially management fee income, and investment income, as being relatively less volatile and as diversifying sources of income.
We principally measure our financial success through long-term growth in tangible book value per common share plus the change in accumulated dividends.

business_model.claim: Consolidated revenues derive principally from net premiums earned, net investment income, and realized and unrealized investment gains or losses; for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, total revenues were 6,654,987, comprising net premiums earned of 6,484,211, net investment income of 1,293,844, equity in earnings of other ventures of 66,853, and other income of 5,740, partially offset by net realized and unrealized investment losses of (1,180,128) and net foreign exchange losses of (15,533) (table in thousands).
quotes: Our revenues are principally derived from three sources: (1) net premiums earned from the reinsurance and insurance policies we sell; (2) net investment income and net realized and unrealized gains from the investment of our capital funds and the investment of the cash we receive on the policies which we sell; and (3) fees received from our joint ventures, managed funds and structured reinsurance products, which are primarily reflected in redeemable noncontrolling interest or as an offset to acquisition or operational expenses.

business_model.basis: stated in P5, P7, F2, and P2
business_model.claim: Through its Capital Partners unit, the company manages joint ventures and funds—including DaVinci, Fontana, Medici, and Vermeer—generating fee income ($81.7 million in the third quarter of 2026) and consolidating full financial results before allocating third-party investors' share through redeemable noncontrolling interests ((688,411) for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, table in thousands).
quotes: Fee income is the income that we earn primarily from managing third-party capital in our Capital Partners unit and is composed of management fee income and performance fee income.

We manage several entities - DaVinci, Fontana, Medici, and Vermeer - where we control the decision making authority through ownership of the voting interests but do not own all of the economic interest.
The remainder, which is ultimately allocated to such third-party investors in those entities, is shown separately in net (income) loss attributable to redeemable noncontrolling interests.

business_model.basis: stated in F1, P2, and P7
business_model.claim: Invested assets totaled 36,191,038 of 54,831,196 total assets at September 30, 2026 (table in thousands), anchored by $ 25,203,247 in fixed maturity investments trading, which produced $440.9 million of net investment income at a 5.8% weighted average yield to maturity in the third quarter of 2026 alongside $879.8 million in mark-to-market losses.
quotes: We have historically derived a meaningful portion of our income from our invested assets, which are principally comprised of fixed maturity securities.

While the Federal Reserve reduced the federal funds target rate in 2025, further increases in interest rates could cause the market value of our investment portfolio to decrease, which could reduce our capital resources over the near-to medium-term.
Conversely, any decline in interest rates could reduce our investment yield and net investment income, which would reduce our overall profitability over the medium- to long-term.

business_model.claim: Major costs consist of net claims and claim expenses incurred, acquisition costs (typically a percentage of premiums written), operational expenses, corporate expenses, interest expense, and income taxes; for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, total expenses were 5,020,429, led by net claims and claim expenses of 2,952,841 and acquisition expenses of 1,628,022, plus operational expenses of 289,382, interest expense of 95,358, and corporate expenses of 54,826 (table in thousands).
quotes: Our expenses primarily consist of: (1) net claims and claim expenses incurred on the policies of reinsurance and insurance we sell; (2) acquisition costs, which typically represent a percentage of the premiums we write; (3) operational expenses, which primarily consist of personnel expenses, rent and other expenses; (4) corporate expenses, which include certain executive, legal and consulting expenses, costs for research and development, transaction and integration-related expenses, and other miscellaneous costs, including those associated with operating as a publicly traded company; (5) interest and dividends related to our debt, preference shares and common shares; and (6) income taxes.

business_model.claim: Underwriting profitability (measured by a combined ratio below 100%) differs sharply by segment: for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, consolidated underwriting income was $1,613,966 (75.1% combined ratio, table in thousands), as Property earned $1,797,161 (31.2% combined ratio) while Casualty and Specialty posted a $(183,195) underwriting loss (104.7% combined ratio).
quotes: The combined ratio is the sum of the net claims and claim expense ratio and the underwriting expense ratio.
A combined ratio below 100% indicates profitable underwriting prior to the consideration of investment income.

business_model.basis: stated in P2, P5, and P7
business_model.claim: Claims costs are heavily driven by natural and non-natural catastrophes, social and economic inflation, and reserve estimation uncertainty; in the third quarter of 2026, large loss events (Middle East War, Ras Laffan Explosion, and Colombian Earthquake) reduced consolidated underwriting results by $(191,449) (table in thousands) and added 9.3 percentage points to the consolidated combined ratio.
quotes: We have substantial exposure to natural and non-natural catastrophic events and circumstances, such as earthquakes, hurricanes, typhoons and tsunamis, winter storms, freezes, floods, fires, tornadoes, hailstorms, drought, pandemics, cyber-risks, political unrest, geopolitical uncertainty and instability, war, riots and acts of terrorism.

We believe that our underwriting results have been adversely impacted over recent periods by increasing fraud and abuses at the primary claims level, as well as other forms of social inflation, and that these trends may continue.

General economic inflation has increased over the past few years compared to recent historical norms, and there is a risk of inflation remaining elevated for an extended period, which could cause claims and claims-related expenses to increase, impact the performance of our investment portfolio, or have other adverse effects.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P2, and F2
business_model.claim: RenaissanceRe purchases reinsurance and retrocessional protection for its own account to optimize its underwriting portfolio, manage regulated-entity capital requirements, and reduce large catastrophe impacts, resulting in 6,620,733 of net premiums written from $ 8,577,305 of gross premiums written in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 (table in thousands).
quotes: We frequently purchase reinsurance or other protection for our own account for a number of reasons, including to optimize the expected outcome of our underwriting portfolio, to manage capital requirements for regulated entities and to reduce the financial impact that a large catastrophe or a series of catastrophes could have on our results.
The retrocessional reinsurance that we purchase for our own account is generally subject to annual renewal.

business_model.claim: Reinsurance pricing and terms are historically cyclical, so the company dynamically expands or contracts its property presence based on market conditions and risk-adjusted pricing adequacy.
quotes: To moderate the volatility of our risk portfolio, we may increase or decrease our presence in the property business based on market conditions and our assessment of risk-adjusted pricing adequacy.
The (re)insurance industry has historically been cyclical by product and market.
We believe the reinsurance industry will remain cyclical, and that we may return to soft market conditions in the future.

business_model.claim: Effective January 1, 2025, Bermuda profits (excluding profits earned by joint ventures and managed funds, though consolidated joint venture and managed fund profits not attributable to redeemable noncontrolling interests are generally expected to be taxed at 15% under Pillar II rules) became subject to a 15% corporate income tax, contributing to (142,231) of income tax expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 (table in thousands).
quotes: Historically, the majority of our income has been earned in Bermuda, which did not have a corporate income tax, so the tax impact to our operations has been minimal.
On December 27, 2023, the Government of Bermuda announced the implementation of a 15% CIT, which became effective on January 1, 2025.
Therefore, our profits generated on or after January 1, 2025 in Bermuda (except for profits earned by our joint ventures and managed funds) are subject to a 15% corporate income tax.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, F3, and P7
business_model.claim: The company prefers deploying excess capital into profitable underwriting opportunities before returning capital to shareholders, and repurchased (1,012,608) of common shares during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 (cash flow table in thousands) plus an additional $143.8 million from October 1, 2026 to October 23, 2026.
quotes: When possible, our preference is to deploy any excess capital into profitable business opportunities before returning excess capital to shareholders.
We repurchased $310.1 million of shares in the third quarter and a further $143.8 million through October 23, 2026, reflecting our commitment to strong capital management.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in Item 1A Risk Factors of the 2025 Form 10-K and confirmed unchanged in Item 1A of the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q.

quotes: The agreements governing our indebtedness require us and/or certain subsidiaries to comply with covenants that impose financial or operational restrictions, including requirements to maintain specific financial ratios or contain cross-default provisions to our other indebtedness.
Failure to comply with these or other covenants could result in an event of default, an acceleration of repayment obligations, cross-default, or a loss of borrowing capacity if not cured or waived.

risks.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 7 MD&A and observed in Q3 2026 10-Q statements of operations.
risks.claim: Bermuda's 15% corporate income tax and Pillar II Rules increase tax burdens on underwriting and investment profits that historically bore minimal tax.
quotes: Historically, the majority of our income has been earned in Bermuda, which did not have a corporate income tax, so the tax impact to our operations has been minimal.
Therefore, our profits generated on or after January 1, 2025 in Bermuda (except for profits earned by our joint ventures and managed funds) are subject to a 15% corporate income tax.

risks.basis: Stated directly in 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
risks.claim: Cyberattacks, third-party system breaches, evolving artificial intelligence risks, and strict data privacy laws threaten operations, regulatory compliance, and cyber-line underwriting results.
quotes: A significant cyber incident, including system failure, security breach, disruption by malware or other damage could interrupt or delay our operations, result in a violation of applicable cybersecurity and privacy and other laws, damage our reputation, cause a loss of customers or expose sensitive customer data, or give rise to monetary fines and other penalties, which could be significant.
We also have exposure to cybersecurity risks through coverage that we write in our cyber line of business.

risks.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1A and Item 7 MD&A, and reiterated in Q3 2026 10-Q Item 2 MD&A.
risks.claim: Elevated inflation could drive higher claims settlement costs and adversely affect investment portfolio performance.
quotes: General economic inflation has increased over the past few years compared to recent historical norms, and there is a risk of inflation remaining elevated for an extended period, which could cause claims and claims-related expenses to increase, impact the performance of our investment portfolio, or have other adverse effects.
The actual effects of the current and potential future increase in inflation on our results cannot be accurately known until, among other items, claims are ultimately settled.

risks.basis: Stated directly in 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
risks.claim: Loss of senior management or Bermuda work permit and immigration restrictions on non-citizen executives could impair strategic execution, customer retention, and capital support.
quotes: The loss of services of members of our senior management team and the uncertain transition of new members of our senior management team may strain our ability to execute our strategic initiatives, or make it more difficult to retain customers, attract or maintain our capital support, or meet other needs of our business.

This risk may be particularly acute for us relative to some of our competitors because some of our senior executives work in countries where they are not citizens (such as Bermuda) and work permit and immigration issues could adversely affect the ability to retain or hire key persons.
